top.title: Packers Injury Report: 9 players limited on Sunday
top.description: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers had their entire active roster available to practice for the second day in a row. Considering how banged up the roster has been this season, that’s a massive win in itself. The Packers didn’t release a Saturday injury report, though, so Sunday was our first look at details on Green Bay’s injuries. Today, the Packers listed cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), linebacker Isaiah McDuffie (rib), receiver Bo Melton (thigh), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) as limited participants. Cisse, Melton and Moore were unable to finish the game against the Minnesota Vikings last week, while Franklin, Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Zeitler never suited up. The only surprise on this list is that McDuffie is still dealing with a rib injury, as he missed just one snap of action against the Vikings and came back into the game. Guard Aaron Banks is listed with only a knee injury, instead of both a knee and groin injury like in previous weeks, and was a full participant on Sunday. According to head coach Matt LaFleur, Banks is competing at both the left guard and right guard positions for playing time this week. If Banks doesn’t earn a starting role in practice, the assumption is that those gigs will go to Laken Tomlinson (left guard) and Kevin Zeitler (right guard). It’s also worth noting that teams are only allowed three padded practices from Week 12 to Week 18 of the NFL regular season. In preparation for their Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, the Packers decided to use a padded practice on Sunday. top.title: Best Case, Worst Case, and Most Likely Scenarios for the 2026-27 Badgers
top.description: MADISON, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 10: Owen Foxwell #15 talks with Head Coach Greg Gard of the Wisconsin Badgers during the second half of the game against the Fairfield Stags at Kohl Center on November 10, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images I waited longer than normal to do this piece because the 2026-27 Wisconsin Badgers carried more uncertainty than usual coming into the season, and I’m glad that I did. The first three weeks of the campaign have been both illuminating and disturbing. One big question coming in was whether or not Wisconsin would effectively replace two premium scorers, John Blackwell and Nick Boyd. We all saw an offensive drop-off on the horizon, but how steep it would be was far from certain. There were also associated worries about the lack of a slasher, along with spooky point guard depth. And, of course, fitting the pieces together has always been a puzzle for Greg Gard, who has generally completed it deftly in recent years. Winning the lottery three consecutive transfer portal cycles certainly helped matters. But as we inch toward December, it is clear that this version of the Badgers is flawed and, after losing Jack Janicki to what could be a long-term injury, is now down a major rotational player. Other issues have been a lack of consistent scoring and an oddly passive start from pre-season All-Big Ten senior Nolan Winter, who is very talented but has, at times, looked disinterested on his way to a tepid 8.0 points per game so far , due to a lack of shooting volume. And while they have had nice moments, it’s hard to be overly excited about portal headliner Eian Elmer or new point guard Owen Foxwell . Both have offered flashes, especially Foxwell, but it hasn’t been nearly enough. Making matters worse, transfer big man Victory Onuetu has looked, at times, unplayable. Adding to all this, nobody appears so far to be better than they were in 2026-27, and team cohesion seems broken, as best evidenced by a forgettable two games at the Baha Mar Championship , where the Badgers were outplayed by two decent but not special teams in Seton Hall and Murray State, never looking comfortable and shooting awfully. So, the quick take is that things are not good for Gard’s team and there is a legitimate reason to worry about an awful season. But Gard is a very good coach, and I suspect he will have some fixes to raise the squad’s suddenly troubling floor. However, nothing is a given. top.title: Mark Pope addresses challenges of roster turnover in modern era, building teams for ‘one-year run’
top.description: Since Mark Pope took over at Kentucky in 2024, the transfer portal has been key to building his rosters. He brought in nine players upon his arrival before adding six transfers during both the 2025 and 2026 cycles. The portal landscape has changed recruiting across college sports since transfers gained immediate eligibility. To Pope, it adds to the challenges of roster construction in the modern era, but he also sees some bright spots. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage In the era of player movement, Pope said it’s harder to tell whether a key piece will still be around through multiple years. While Trent Noah is still with the Kentucky program from Pope’s first class, he knows “one-year runs” are becoming more apparent as teams build rosters. “We’re in this era where seasons are standalones,” Pope told Jon Rothstein . “Of course, with everything that changes, you miss some things – you used to be putting together a roster that you would plan out who is going to be around, a particular player, three years from now. There was something great about that and seeing guys grow that way. Listen, we still have third-year guys here at Kentucky that have been with me the whole time. SUBSCRIBE to the On3 NIL and Sports Business Newsletter “But you really, in some essence now, are reconstructing a team for a one-year run in some senses. There’s some really magical things about that, too, is knowing that this is your shot. This is the year that you guys get to be together as an entire group. Taking advantage of every moment and the pace of growth and development and learning, those challenges are really exciting, too.” Last year’s Kentucky team drew plenty of headlines with a roster that reportedly cost upward of $22 million. The Wildcats went 22-24 and lost to Iowa State in the second round of the NCAA Tournament, one year after making it to the Sweet Sixteen in Pope’s debut season. As a result, the 2026-27 season became a big one for Mark Pope in Year 3 at his alma mater, where he was a captain for Rick Pitino . There have been some missteps through the early going, though, as Kentucky heads into Thanksgiving with a 4-2 record. The Wildcats lost to Kansas by 20 points during the Champions Classic and, most recently, had a rough second half in a 90-76 loss to Indiana . They also found themselves in a nail-biter against Northern Arizona at Rupp Arena before coming away with the 78-77 win.

The Steelers had a fairly favorable path to end a decades-long losing streak in Philadelphia. Instead, they lost their 12th consecutive road game against the Eagles, dating back to 1965. Facing an Eagles team down to its third quarterback, dealing with injuries and subtractions at multiple key positions, the Steelers fell 19-16 on Sunday, unable to generate much offense due to five sacks against Aaron Rodgers and an ejection for DK Metcalf. As Joe Milton did just enough to get Philadelphia a win — its first since Week 2 — Pittsburgh dropped a game that could have some lasting consequences in its AFC playoff chase. Here's an updated look at the Steelers' path to the playoffs after losing to the Eagles. Had the Steelers won in Week 11, they would have remained tied in the win column with the Bengals at the top of the AFC North, with Cincinnati still to play on Monday night against the Commanders. Instead, if the Bengals beat Washington on Monday, the Steelers will be two full games behind in the division. top.title: ‘Honestly baffling’ – Josh Allen blasted for ‘reckless’ performance in Bills win vs Dolphins
top.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images Josh Allen has come under fire for his shaky performance in the Buffalo Bills’ 26-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon. Allen threw two interceptions against the Bills’ struggling AFC rivals and a third was overturned for a penalty. The 30-year-old finished the game with just one passing touchdown as Buffalo improved to 10-1. His display raised questions about his passing form, particularly against a Dolphins team sitting at 1-8 before this weekend. NFL fans voiced their frustration with the Bills star on social media. One wrote: “Josh Allen hasn’t been a good passer or processor from the pocket for like two years now. It’s honestly baffling.” Another added: “ Josh Allen throwing 3 first-half INTs is nasty work. That 3rd one got called back, but man, the decision-making has been reckless”. A third posted: “Josh Allen has 2 picks against a bad team, with a bad defense, that is also starting a backup QB.” Others were equally unimpressed, with one fan describing it as “Probably Josh Allen’s worst game since the Dolphins game last year.” Another declared: “Safe to say Josh Allen won’t win MVP this season.” Allen has remained in the MVP conversation largely because of Buffalo’s impressive record and his contributions as a runner. He has scored 11 rushing touchdowns this season, but his passing numbers of 14 touchdowns and nine interceptions have not been as convincing. A win is a win for Buffalo, but Allen will need more consistent performances through the air if he is to remain a serious contender for the MVP award. The Bills now face a blockbuster Thanksgiving weekend showdown against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. top.title: Jeeno Thitikul three-peats at CME, earning another $4 million check
top.description: NAPLES, FL — Jeeno Thitikul has become a money-making machine . The world No. 2 became the first player to three-peat at the CME Group Tour Championship . In fact, she's the first player to win a tournament three times in a row since Inbee Park won what's now the KPMG Women's PGA from 2013-2015. "I have no word(s)," said Thitikul after a closing 7-under 65 at Tiburón Golf Club. "The only word I have to Terry [Duffy] is just don't change the course until I retire. Don't change it. I mean, it's just me and the course. I think we just really best friend." With the victory, 23-year-old Thitikul surpasses Annika Sorenstam on the all-time money list with $24,292,858. She earned nearly half of that in only three starts at the CME. Nelly Korda, who played alongside Thitikul on Sunday, finished solo third after a closing 68. The world No. 1 also surpassed Sorenstam with a $550,000 check. Korda's career earnings are now $22,972,616. Thitikul, who joined the tour in 2022, accomplishes the feat in only 104 career starts. Sorenstam retired in 2008 and won 72 times. She reached $22,583,693 in 308 starts. "It's really hard to go up against Jeeno out here," said Korda, who has yet to win at Tiburon. "I feel like she just has this place figured out." A victory today at CME would've put Korda into the LPGA Hall of Fame as she's only one point shy of the 27 required to gain entry. Korda won four times this season, including the U.S. Women's Open and Chevron Championship , to earn the LPGA's Rolex Player of the Year award. She battled a two-way miss throughout the week at Tiburon. "You know, still being able to compete when I didn't even really feel like I really had my trust in like a B or C game," she said of her main takeaways. "So just proud of the way that I fought this week to kind of give myself a chance." Thitikul won a tour-leading five times on the LPGA this season, including at home in Thailand, the place where it all began. She made 18 cuts in 20 starts, finishing in the top 10 a total of 11 times (including the wins). The CME check brings her season earnings to $6,923,458. Though she has yet to win a major, Thitikul has said many times throughout her career that her primary goal was to take care of her family, and she has provided well with 12 career victories. Thitikul finished at 24 under for the tournament, two strokes ahead of Japan's Aki Iwai (65), who still won $1 million for her efforts. Miyu Yamashita, a three-time winner this season, won the Vare Trophy with a 69.453 scoring average. Both Nelly Korda and Haeran Ryu were ineligible after failing to meet the required minimum number of rounds. "I'm truly honored to receive this award," said Yamashita. "My goal this season was to win, and I managed to win three times, so overall it's been really good year for me." LOS ANGELES — With Thanksgiving around the corner, baseball fans have plenty to be thankful for. However, the holiday season isn't the only thing on the minds of Major League Baseball fans. The countdown to a potential MLB lockout is quickly approaching, with the current collective bargaining agreement set to expire on December 1, 2026. Unless the league and the MLB Players Association reach an agreement, a lockout could begin December 2, bringing baseball's offseason to a sudden halt. The biggest disagreement between the two sides remains the possibility of introducing a salary cap and floor. Owners are pushing for a system that could take effect as early as 2028, while the MLBPA continues to strongly oppose a salary cap. The timing couldn't be worse for teams looking to make significant offseason moves. With Opening Night scheduled for March 24, 2027, and spring training traditionally beginning in mid-to-late February, a prolonged labor dispute could put the upcoming season in jeopardy. If negotiations stretch too far into March, the possibility of losing regular-season games, or even threatening the full 162-game schedule, becomes increasingly real. For now, teams still have an opportunity to make trades and sign free agents before a potential lockout prevents further transactions. And the Dodgers aren't wasting any time. Following a disappointing end to their season, in which they were swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS, the Dodgers are looking to make the necessary adjustments to get back to the top of baseball. top.title: Connor Hellebuyck Hid the Winnipeg Jets’ Biggest Problem for Years. Kyle Connor Is Doing It Again
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kyle Connor has scored 19 of the Winnipeg Jets’ 75 goals this season. That’s 25.3% of the team’s offense through 24 games, which is a pretty ridiculous number for one player to be responsible for. It’s also the sort of statistic that should make Jets fans a little uncomfortable. Connor is doing his job. He’s one of the NHL’s best goal scorers, he’s scoring like one, and nobody is going to complain about having a player who can put the puck in the net almost whenever he feels like it. But when one guy is responsible for more than a quarter of your goals, you have to wonder what happens when he stops scoring at this pace. For Jets fans, this should sound familiar. They spent years watching Connor Hellebuyck turn games the Jets had no business winning into two points in the standings. Sometimes the Jets were genuinely excellent. Other nights, Hellebuyck was the reason nobody cared that they weren’t. The results were great. The problem was figuring out how much of that success was sustainable without him. Now Hellebuyck is in New Jersey, Connor is doing his best to carry the offense, and the Jets are still having trouble controlling play at five-on-five. The more you dig into the team’s numbers from the past several seasons, the harder it becomes to ignore just how much Hellebuyck was making up for. Hellebuyck Was Outperforming Expectations Even When the Jets Weren’t There’s a statistic from the Jets’ 2022-23 season that deserves a lot more attention than it’s received. The Jets finished that year with a plus-11 goal differential at five-on-five, slightly worse than their expected differential of plus-11.55. Nothing especially remarkable there. They scored about as many goals relative to their opponents as the quality of chances suggested they should have. Except Hellebuyck personally saved 22.46 goals above expected. That’s 22.46 goals he prevented beyond what the quality of chances he faced would predict, and the Jets still finished slightly below their expected goal differential as a team. It wasn’t the only time. In 2021-22, the Jets finished 4.95 goals below their expected differential despite Hellebuyck saving 6.28 goals above expected. In 2025-26, the team finished 0.89 goals below expected while Hellebuyck saved another 9.42. Three seasons in which the Jets failed to outperform their expected goal differential despite their starting goaltender beating expectations individually. And when the rest of the team was playing well? That’s when things got ridiculous. The Jets’ Presidents’ Trophy Season Wasn’t Quite What It Looked Like The 2024-25 Jets won 56 games, finished first overall and had the NHL’s best power play. Hellebuyck won the Hart and Vezina trophies, Mark Scheifele scored 39 goals and Connor recorded 97 points. It was the best regular season in Jets 2.0 history, and anybody trying to dismiss 56 wins is being silly. But the Jets’ five-on-five results were considerably better than their underlying number

nigeria.title: ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 4-0 loss
nigeria.description: Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card. Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak. United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick. Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974. “It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino. “We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.” Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro. “I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino. “At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.” – ‘Changes the game completely’ – A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes. However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half. “It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro. “There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international. “It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.” Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal. Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory. Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time. “It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola. “We have missed some clear chances today. nigeria.title: CJN tasks lawyers to embrace scholarship
nigeria.description: …Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law books By Innocent Anaba LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resources that will enrich Nigerian jurisprudence and strengthen the intellectual foundation of the legal profession. Kekere-Ekun, who spoke, weekend, while chairing the public presentation of the books in Lagos, said the publications reflected an impressive combination of legal scholarship, practical experience and engagement with contemporary developments in the administration of justice. She noted that the collection, comprising four books authored by Pinheiro and two compilations produced in his honour, addressed significant areas of legal practice, including litigation, arbitration, insolvency, criminal law, technology and contemporary jurisprudence. According to her, the publications were not merely a collection of books assembled to commemorate an accomplished legal practitioner but works that sought to make legal knowledge more accessible and useful to those responsible for applying, interpreting and developing the law. The CJN said: “Taken together, the works reflect an engagement with important areas of legal practice and scholarship, as well as an attempt to preserve the experiences and contributions of a distinguished member of our profession.” Kekere-Ekun described ‘Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk’ as particularly significant because it offered a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar. She observed that memoirs of this nature were valuable because they preserved aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records. Such accounts, she said, enabled younger practitioners to appreciate the human experiences behind professional milestones, including the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompanied a successful legal career. The CJN also highlighted the importance of the two publications on arbitration and insolvency, particularly against the background of Nigeria’s increasingly sophisticated business environment and the need for effective legal responses to commercial transactions. , financial distress and dispute resolution. Similarly, she described Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure as an important contribution to an increasingly relevant area of law under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. According to her, its examination of corporate rescue, restructuring, administration and other mechanisms for addressing financial distress reflected the growing recognition that preserving viable businesses could, in appropriate circumstances, better serve creditors, employees, investors and the wider economy than immediate liquidation.

nigeria.title: 2027: Any party saying I’ve stepped down is working for Tinubu - Atiku
nigeria.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused political parties spreading claims that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race of working in favour of President Bola Tinubu. Atiku described the reports as false and insisted that he remained in the contest to win the election. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice-president said no group claiming to be his supporters had the authority to announce his withdrawal. “Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field,” he said. Atiku added that he had not made any decision to leave the race, dismissing claims attributed to individuals presenting themselves as his supporters. “Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision,” he said. He warned that any attempt to remove him from the contest through fabricated declarations would deny Nigerians the opportunity to choose their preferred candidate. “If I am not on the ballot, Bola Tinubu might as well wait for a coronation. But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice,” he said. The former vice-president also accused those behind the reports of using misinformation to weaken the opposition, alleging that the tactic was intended to benefit the ruling All Progressives Congress. He urged opposition parties seeking to defeat Tinubu to focus on persuading voters rather than circulating claims about rival candidates. “Anyone serious about defeating the APC should take their case to voters. Manufacturing supporters and circulating false declarations will not defeat Tinubu. It only serves him,” Atiku said. On his campaign activities, Atiku said his Affordable Life agenda remained focused on addressing the economic difficulties confronting Nigerian households. He cited the rising cost of food and transportation as issues his campaign intended to address, saying the campaign was reaching communities across the country. “Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport,” he said. Atiku urged his supporters to remain mobilised ahead of the election and ensure they had their Permanent Voter Cards. He reiterated that he would not withdraw in favour of any other candidate, declaring that the contest would be decided by voters. “I do not need anyone to step down for me, and I am stepping down for no one,” he said. The statement concluded with Atiku expressing confidence that he would defeat Tinubu at the ballot box on January 16, 2027. nigeria.title: Horror in Calabar: Driver runs over Nursing student twice, flees
nigeria.description: By Emma Una CALABAR—A nursing student of the School of Nursing, Mary Slessor Avenue, Calabar, identified as Cynthia Eni, has been killed after a speeding driver reportedly knocked her down and reversed to run over her a second time before fleeing the scene. The incident, which occurred at the weekend, happened as Cynthia was crossing the road into the school compound after going out with two colleagues to buy some items. A friend of the deceased, Mercy, who witnessed the incident, said the driver first knocked Cynthia down before reversing and running over her again as people attempted to come to her rescue. “It was a bewildering scene. When the car knocked her down, we were shouting for help and before some boys could rush down, the same car returned and climbed her again. When the car was approaching we thought the driver had come to help but was surprised when the car ran over her again.” Mercy said the driver took advantage of the fading light and the fact that people were focused on the victim to escape, adding that the vehicle’s registration number was not visible. She said Cynthia, who was about 30, had completed her Community Health studies at the College of Health Technology and enrolled at the School of Nursing to obtain an additional qualification. “We don’t know what was in the driver’s mind. Even if he was drunk or had some issues with Cynthia, he should have had some sense of humanity and not come back to crush her the way he did.” Mercy said she could not recall any misunderstanding between the deceased and fellow students or outsiders. “We leave everything to God,” she said, breaking down in tears. There was no official at the Provost’s Office available to comment on the incident as it occurred at the weekend. nigeria.title: Bayelsa Boat Mishap: Death toll rises to 29
nigeria.description: …Tinubu approves N250m for victims’ families, directs NDDC to procure boats …FG backs probe of incident …Diri makes case for senatorial roads By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The death toll from last Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with more than 51 survivors recorded, as search and recovery operations continue. President Bola Tinubu has also approved N250 million to support families of the victims and directed the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) to procure boats to improve water transportation in the riverine communities. Vice President Kashim Shettima announced the presidential intervention on Sunday during a condolence visit to Bayelsa State on the President’s directive. The boat, which was conveying passengers to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony, capsized near Oweikorogha community, leaving several persons dead and others rescued. Speaking at the Government House, Yenagoa, after visiting hospitalised survivors at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital (BMUTH), Shettima said the President had directed relevant federal agencies to collaborate with the state government in the search and rescue operations and provide support for those affected. He described the incident as a national tragedy, noting that behind the casualty figures were individuals with families, relationships and responsibilities to their communities and society. “Each person involved has a name, an identity, a history, relationships and responsibilities. Family members cannot come to terms with the fact that someone who left home for a funeral will never return,” he said. The Vice President acknowledged the peculiar geographical challenges of Bayelsa, where waterways serve as major transportation routes connecting communities to schools, hospitals, markets and other essential services. “Geography can determine how people travel, but it will never determine the worth of the lives involved,” Shettima stated. He disclosed that Tinubu had directed the NDDC to procure boats to improve transportation in the riverine areas of the state. Shettima also commended Governor Douye Diri for his response to the tragedy and the establishment of a commission of inquiry to investigate the incident. Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? sports.title: Packers Injury Report: 9 players limited on Sunday
sports.description: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers had their entire active roster available to practice for the second day in a row. Considering how banged up the roster has been this season, that’s a massive win in itself. The Packers didn’t release a Saturday injury report, though, so Sunday was our first look at details on Green Bay’s injuries. Today, the Packers listed cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), linebacker Isaiah McDuffie (rib), receiver Bo Melton (thigh), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) as limited participants. Cisse, Melton and Moore were unable to finish the game against the Minnesota Vikings last week, while Franklin, Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Zeitler never suited up. The only surprise on this list is that McDuffie is still dealing with a rib injury, as he missed just one snap of action against the Vikings and came back into the game. Guard Aaron Banks is listed with only a knee injury, instead of both a knee and groin injury like in previous weeks, and was a full participant on Sunday. According to head coach Matt LaFleur, Banks is competing at both the left guard and right guard positions for playing time this week. If Banks doesn’t earn a starting role in practice, the assumption is that those gigs will go to Laken Tomlinson (left guard) and Kevin Zeitler (right guard). It’s also worth noting that teams are only allowed three padded practices from Week 12 to Week 18 of the NFL regular season. The first three weeks of the campaign have been both illuminating and disturbing. One big question coming in was whether or not Wisconsin would effectively replace two premium scorers, John Blackwell and Nick Boyd. We all saw an offensive drop-off on the horizon, but how steep it would be was far from certain. There were also associated worries about the lack of a slasher, along with spooky point guard depth. And, of course, fitting the pieces together has always been a puzzle for Greg Gard, who has generally completed it deftly in recent years. Winning the lottery three consecutive transfer portal cycles certainly helped matters. But as we inch toward December, it is clear that this version of the Badgers is flawed and, after losing Jack Janicki to what could be a long-term injury, is now down a major rotational player. Other issues have been a lack of consistent scoring and an oddly passive start from pre-season All-Big Ten senior Nolan Winter, who is very talented but has, at times, looked disinterested on his way to a tepid 8.0 points per game so far , due to a lack of shooting volume. And while they have had nice moments, it’s hard to be overly excited about portal headliner Eian Elmer or new point guard Owen Foxwell . sports.title: Jeeno Thitikul three-peats at CME, earning another $4 million check
sports.description: NAPLES, FL — Jeeno Thitikul has become a money-making machine . The world No. 2 became the first player to three-peat at the CME Group Tour Championship . In fact, she's the first player to win a tournament three times in a row since Inbee Park won what's now the KPMG Women's PGA from 2013-2015. "I have no word(s)," said Thitikul after a closing 7-under 65 at Tiburón Golf Club. "The only word I have to Terry [Duffy] is just don't change the course until I retire. Don't change it. I mean, it's just me and the course. I think we just really best friend." With the victory, 23-year-old Thitikul surpasses Annika Sorenstam on the all-time money list with $24,292,858. She earned nearly half of that in only three starts at the CME. Nelly Korda, who played alongside Thitikul on Sunday, finished solo third after a closing 68. The world No. 1 also surpassed Sorenstam with a $550,000 check. Korda's career earnings are now $22,972,616. Thitikul, who joined the tour in 2022, accomplishes the feat in only 104 career starts. Sorenstam retired in 2008 and won 72 times. She reached $22,583,693 in 308 starts. "It's really hard to go up against Jeeno out here," said Korda, who has yet to win at Tiburon. "I feel like she just has this place figured out." A victory today at CME would've put Korda into the LPGA Hall of Fame as she's only one point shy of the 27 required to gain entry. Korda won four times this season, including the U.S. Women's Open and Chevron Championship , to earn the LPGA's Rolex Player of the Year award. She battled a two-way miss throughout the week at Tiburon. "You know, still being able to compete when I didn't even really feel like I really had my trust in like a B or C game," she said of her main takeaways. "So just proud of the way that I fought this week to kind of give myself a chance." Thitikul won a tour-leading five times on the LPGA this season, including at home in Thailand, the place where it all began. She made 18 cuts in 20 starts, finishing in the top 10 a total of 11 times (including the wins). The CME check brings her season earnings to $6,923,458. Though she has yet to win a major, Thitikul has said many times throughout her career that her primary goal was to take care of her family, and she has provided well with 12 career victories. Thitikul finished at 24 under for the tournament, two strokes ahead of Japan's Aki Iwai (65), who still won $1 million for her efforts. Miyu Yamashita, a three-time winner this season, won the Vare Trophy with a 69.453 scoring average. Both Nelly Korda and Haeran Ryu were ineligible after failing to meet the required minimum number of rounds. "I'm truly honored to receive this award," said Yamashita. "My goal this season was to win, and I managed to win three times, so overall it's been really good year for me." Beth Ann Nichols is a senior writer for Golfweek covering the LPGA and all things women's golf. Follow her on X/Twitter (@GolfweekNichols). This article originally appeared on Golfweek: J

LOS ANGELES — With Thanksgiving around the corner, baseball fans have plenty to be thankful for. However, the holiday season isn't the only thing on the minds of Major League Baseball fans. The countdown to a potential MLB lockout is quickly approaching, with the current collective bargaining agreement set to expire on December 1, 2026. Unless the league and the MLB Players Association reach an agreement, a lockout could begin December 2, bringing baseball's offseason to a sudden halt. The biggest disagreement between the two sides remains the possibility of introducing a salary cap and floor. Owners are pushing for a system that could take effect as early as 2028, while the MLBPA continues to strongly oppose a salary cap. The timing couldn't be worse for teams looking to make significant offseason moves. With Opening Night scheduled for March 24, 2027, and spring training traditionally beginning in mid-to-late February, a prolonged labor dispute could put the upcoming season in jeopardy. If negotiations stretch too far into March, the possibility of losing regular-season games, or even threatening the full 162-game schedule, becomes increasingly real. For now, teams still have an opportunity to make trades and sign free agents before a potential lockout prevents further transactions. And the Dodgers aren't wasting any time. Following a disappointing end to their season, in which they were swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS, the Dodgers are looking to make the necessary adjustments to get back to the top of baseball. sports.title: Connor Hellebuyck Hid the Winnipeg Jets’ Biggest Problem for Years. Kyle Connor Is Doing It Again
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kyle Connor has scored 19 of the Winnipeg Jets’ 75 goals this season. That’s 25.3% of the team’s offense through 24 games, which is a pretty ridiculous number for one player to be responsible for. It’s also the sort of statistic that should make Jets fans a little uncomfortable. Connor is doing his job. He’s one of the NHL’s best goal scorers, he’s scoring like one, and nobody is going to complain about having a player who can put the puck in the net almost whenever he feels like it. But when one guy is responsible for more than a quarter of your goals, you have to wonder what happens when he stops scoring at this pace. For Jets fans, this should sound familiar. They spent years watching Connor Hellebuyck turn games the Jets had no business winning into two points in the standings. Sometimes the Jets were genuinely excellent. Other nights, Hellebuyck was the reason nobody cared that they weren’t. The results were great. The problem was figuring out how much of that success was sustainable without him. Now Hellebuyck is in New Jersey, Connor is doing his best to carry the offense, and the Jets are still having trouble controlling play at five-on-five. The more you dig into the team’s numbers from the past several seasons, the harder it becomes to ignore just how much Hellebuyck was making up for. Hellebuyck Was Outperforming Expectations Even When the Jets Weren’t There’s a statistic from the Jets’ 2022-23 season that deserves a lot more attention than it’s received. The Jets finished that year with a plus-11 goal differential at five-on-five, slightly worse than their expected differential of plus-11.55. Nothing especially remarkable there. They scored about as many goals relative to their opponents as the quality of chances suggested they should have. Except Hellebuyck personally saved 22.46 goals above expected. That’s 22.46 goals he prevented beyond what the quality of chances he faced would predict, and the Jets still finished slightly below their expected goal differential as a team. It wasn’t the only time. In 2021-22, the Jets finished 4.95 goals below their expected differential despite Hellebuyck saving 6.28 goals above expected. In 2025-26, the team finished 0.89 goals below expected while Hellebuyck saved another 9.42. Three seasons in which the Jets failed to outperform their expected goal differential despite their starting goaltender beating expectations individually. And when the rest of the team was playing well? That’s when things got ridiculous. The Jets’ Presidents’ Trophy Season Wasn’t Quite What It Looked Like The 2024-25 Jets won 56 games, finished first overall and had the NHL’s best power play. Hellebuyck won the Hart and Vezina trophies, Mark Scheifele scored 39 goals and Connor recorded 97 points. It was the best regular season in Jets 2.0 history, and anybody trying to dismiss 56 wins is being silly. But the Jets’ five-on-five results were considerably better than their underlying number

sports.description: The Baltimore Ravens lost their sixth straight game on Sunday afternoon, falling to the Carolina Panthers by a score of 35-33. A back-and-forth matchup came down to the final drives, and once again, Baltimore’s defense could not get off the field during a late drive with the game on the line. Carolina took a two-point lead, setting Jacoby Brissett up for a potential game-winning score. Instead, he faced constant pressure in the pocket and had to throw up a prayer to avoid a sack that resulted in a game-ending interception. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the loss: Nikhil Mehta This game was drunk from the very start. The Ravens made their usual mistakes in all three phases – missed tackles, poor clock management, inept pass protection – but the Panthers tried to outdo them at every turn. There aren’t really any new takeaways. As in 2025, this team has been screaming at us, all year, that this is who they are. Jesse Minter’s Ravens simply cannot be at their best when the best is needed. In my opinion, their best is no longer needed. At 4-7, the season is effectively over. Winning out to snag a playoff spot – if that is even possible – is far-fetched even if Lamar Jackson comes back against the Steelers in Week 15. In fact, far-fetched might not be far enough. technology.description: The computerization of cars comes at a price to US consumers, according to the Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), which says that software fees and other charges faced by mechanics push up garage costs. An investigation by the non-profit consumer group estimates that car repair costs for Americans have been inflated by $12 billion each year, as vehicles integrate more computerized functions. Its report, Closing Shop , is available online. To find a failed sensor, release an electronic parking brake, or perform diagnostics, a technician has to first connect a laptop or tablet to the vehicle. To so this, the repair shop has to have the right software tools, and that means paying the vehicle manufacturer subscription charges and other fees, in order to get the information they need to complete the job. If smaller independent repair shops can’t afford all the necessary software or subscriptions, they may be forced to steer customers to authorized dealerships for some fixes – about one in five jobs – and this allows the latter to charge more. PIRG claims that drivers pay for this through their insurance premiums, even if they never need to get their car fixed, because higher repair costs mean higher insurance claims. It says the price of auto insurance has risen three times as fast as the rest of the US economy since 2012. Even if mechanics do choose to pay for the software, they spend an estimated collective 83 million hours a year buying, downloading, logging in, and waiting. At typical repair rates, that adds up to $12 billion. A separate report from the PIRG Education Fund claims that a two-tiered repair model now exists, where independent sites conduct repairs with less information, less powerful diagnostic tools, and higher associated costs than the authorized dealerships. The advocacy group wants to see legislators take this issue in hand, and has a number of recommendations for them. One is to stop manufacturers from locking out independent mechanics from simple repair jobs like changing brake pads, and require them to support a standard protocol for authenticating independent diagnostic tools. Another is to give owners control over their vehicle’s data via a standardized platform for accessing telematics repair information, so that the owner can give access to an independent repair shop. Car firms can use the vehicle data to tell owners that a repair is needed and to take it to an approved repair shop, without even disclosing what the issue is. science.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
science.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

science.title: SpaceX sends classified US spy satellites to orbit in early-morning launch from California coast (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the NROL-136 mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office from California on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the U.S. Space Force , and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 is the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes , in his feature film debut, " First Contact " consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved. science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo mission becomes 2nd ever to arrive in orbit around Mercury
science.description: null Update for 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 22: On Sunday afternoon (Nov. 22), the BepiColombo team announced that, while the spacecraft did successfully arrive in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), things didn't go entirely according to plan. "During the manoeuvre, the thruster burn was shorter than planned due to a software issue," the mission team said via X . "The spacecraft is safe & teams at ESOC are working to understand what happened. Updates provided on Monday." For just the second time ever, Mercury has received a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — arrived in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. Before BepiColombo, just one spacecraft had ever circled the solar system's innermost planet: NASA's MESSENGER , which did so from March 2011 to April 2015. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must therefore shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Saturday's orbital insertion came after a 37-minute-long engine burn, which began at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT). There was a bit drama involved, however, as confirmation of the maneuver's success didn't come for several hours afterward. "We've heard back from Bepi — the spacecraft is now in contact with the ground and the teams at ESOC [the European Space Operations Centre] are busy assessing the telemetry. science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads. NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies.
